newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end firm in heavy trade on re-election.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end firm in heavy trade on re-election.

text.p: Brazil stocks closed strong in high turnover on Tuesday as optimism grew that a bill allowing presidential re-election will be approved in Congress despite delays and setbacks in the voting, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares ended up 2.83 percent or 2,093 points, with market volume totalling a heavy 645.2 million reais ($619.4 million).
Market mood changed as the government moved to overcome resistance to re-election within Congress' largest party, analysts said.
"Today's performance reflects optimism over the latest developments in Brasilia," said Alfredo Rizkallah, president of the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).

A scheduled vote in a lower house committee on Tuesday was postponed until Wednesday, which was seen as giving members of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) more time to sort out their differences.

Government's efforts to get a quick approval of the re-election amendment suffered a blow on Sunday when the PMDB recommended that its members should delay a vote on the bill until February 15 and then reject it.

Rizkallah said the outlook for re-election also improved with the possibility of a referendum being called to discuss the re-election. A plebiscite would be the government's response to an eventual rejection of the bill by lawmakers.
In addition to the re-election issue, the Bovespa chief said a rise on Wall Street contributed to push share prices higher.
Traders noted all top blue-chips posted strong gains on Tuesday.
Benchmark Telebras rose 2.82 percent to 87.50 reais, while state oil firm Petrobras soared 5.93 percent to close at 187.50 reais.
State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce jumped 4.07 percent despite a company denial of a news report saying it had made a new gold and copper discovery.
Analysts said remarks by Planning Minister Antonio Kandir that the firm will be privatized in the first quarter overshadowed the company's denial.
Power stocks also ended firm, with Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig leading the rally by surging 5.2 percent to 42.50 reais.
The power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, rose 3.07 percent to close at 2,197 points.
